title: Paragraphed Index Entries with Subentries

illustrates.quote: Transcribe indexes printed in two or more columns as a list. Do not retain column headings. Insert a transcriber’s note to explain the change to print format.

items.text: growth of real per capita personal income, 399

print.printFeatures: A nested index list: main entries in cell 1, subentries in cell 3, all runovers at cell 5.

braille.notes: Re-extracted from source: the given run's braille.lines wrongly included the 'Example 21-14: ...' title and 4 leading blank lines; the source's own instruction directly above this example ('Change subentries in paragraph form to a nested list. Start main entries in cell 1. All runovers are in the same position.') is the actual rule text this example illustrates — not a bare rule id, so illustrates.rule cites 21.4.2 (indexes printed with subentries — nested-list transcription) and the quote is that instruction.

resolution: print.blocks rebuilt from A/B's own paragraph-form text as the nested index list the source's own instruction describes (the paragraph form was itself a restatement of the SOURCE instruction text, not print content to transcribe); braille.lines corrected: removed 5 bogus leading lines (title + 4 blanks); illustrates.rule set to 21.4.2 (the actual governing rule; A/B's own 'rule' field just repeated the instruction sentence). The first two subentries' own page numbers are embedded directly in item text with a literal trailing semicolon (not the `page` field, which has no way to add trailing punctuation AFTER the page number it appends) — the given braille keeps the print's own semicolon-joined single run-in list, one subentry per braille line.
